title: Celtics ‘expressed interest’ in LeBron James in free agency before he joined 76ers
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Boston Celtics expressed interest in free agent LeBron James before he signed with the Philadelphia 76ers.
LeBron James left the Lakers after eight years, signing with the 76ers who also acquired Jaylen Brown.
James signed a two-year deal with a player's option, joining a 76ers roster including Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey.

title: Parts of Mass. under flash flood warning as state sees heavy rain
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Flash flood warning issued for Western Massachusetts, including Springfield, Chicopee, and Westfield, until 6 p.m. Wednesday.
Berkshire County faces a flood warning until 5:45 p.m. with expected rainfall of up to 7 inches.
Central and Western Massachusetts, Eastern Rhode Island, and Connecticut are under flood watch until 8 p.m. Wednesday.

title: Cyclist, 39, killed in Stoughton crash
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Mark Salvador, 39, of Stoughton, died after being struck by a vehicle on Route 138 Wednesday morning.
Stoughton police received the report of the crash shortly after 5 a.m. near 1378 Washington St.
The investigation is ongoing; no details about the driver or potential charges have been released.

title: Wu unveiled a street safety plan after a cyclist was killed. Transit advocates say it doesn’t go far enough.
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Mayor Wu proposed street safety improvements after cyclist Louisa Gag was killed by a truck on Tremont Street.
Transit advocates criticize the plan for lacking specific timelines and accountability for delayed safety projects.
Wu's initiatives include monthly updates to the Vision Zero dashboard and installing quick-build barriers by year-end.

title: What to know about the Green Line shutdowns planned for August
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: The MBTA plans August Green Line shutdowns for tunnel upgrades and accessibility improvements.
From August 8-16, service is suspended on B, C, D, and E branches, replaced by free shuttle buses.
Riders should expect up to 25 extra minutes in travel time and plan commutes accordingly.

title: Suffolk corrections officer killed after stopping to help stranded motorist in Boxford
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Brett Martin, 51, was killed after being struck by a vehicle while assisting a stranded motorist on I-95 in Boxford.
Massachusetts State Police responded at 8:30 p.m.; Martin was found with life-threatening injuries and later died at a hospital.
The Essex County District Attorney’s Office is investigating the incident; Martin served in the Suffolk County Sheriff’s Department since 2008.

title: Review & setlist: Tame Impala reimagines the bounds of arena rock at TD Garden
author: Perry Eaton
bullets: Tame Impala performed the first of two sold-out shows at TD Garden, featuring a 360-degree stage setup.
Opener Djo, led by Joe Keery from Newburyport, delivered a well-received set featuring songs from his album 'The Crux.'
The performance included highlights like 'The Less I Know the Better' and new tracks like 'Dracula' from the album 'Deadbeat.'

title: Electric utility rates are going up Aug. 1. Will your bill actually increase?
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Starting August 1, National Grid, Eversource, and Unitil are raising supply rates due to market conditions.
26.6% of Massachusetts electric customers on basic service will experience the increase, while most use alternative suppliers.
State reports indicate competitive suppliers have led to higher costs for customers compared to basic service rates.

title: Man called in bomb threat after getting kicked out of Boston movie theater, police say
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Christopher McFadden, 55, was arrested for making a bomb threat at an AMC theater in Boston.
McFadden allegedly threatened a theater manager with sharpened chopsticks before leaving the premises.
A phone in McFadden's possession matched the number used for the bomb threat, confirming his involvement.

title: In new ‘milestone,’ Rhode Island nonprofit tags first hammerhead shark
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: The Atlantic Shark Institute tagged its first hammerhead shark near Block Island, marking a new milestone for the Rhode Island nonprofit.
Climate change is allowing typically southern shark species, like hammerheads, to move into the warmer waters off New England.
The institute's tagging program, using satellite and acoustic tags, helps track shark migrations and habitat usage over the long term.
